items.title: Chuck Israels interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 11, 2021
items.q: I just wanted to ask you about, just a little bit about your time with Bill Evans... This was written about Scott LaFaro... you didn’t feel any pressure to like try to recreate what he was doing? ... I was playing music like that... Scotty wasn’t alone... I was playing music like that

ctx.x: No. I didn’t get that far. I was — some people have, when I’ve talked to them about this have excused me, probably realistically, by saying, “Of course you were focused on a particular thing. You were trying to understand and become conversant in the language of Bill Evans, Tommy Flanagan, Hank Jones, Sonny Clark were the piano players for example. And the piano playing language of Monk was so — at least superficially — diametrically opposed to that, that you couldn’t take it in. You couldn’t see — that was…

All right. I wanted to ask you about, just a little bit about your time with Bill Evans. And I saw you say that when you got that gig, which of course was under unfortunate circumstances but nonetheless you felt you were going to get it. This was written about Scott LaFaro well after the fact in the New Grove Dictionary it said, “Scott set the © Fillius Jazz Archive -10-

standard for new generations of jazz bass players who varied their accompaniment by mixing traditional timekeeping with far-ranging countermelodies in free rhythm.” Now I don’t know if at that time people would have written that or if it’s in retrospect, but you didn’t feel any pressure to like try to recreate what he was doing?
